claims.note: REJECTED. The verifier quoted only the continuation of the sentence, which resumes on the next page of R47106 ("separate regular appropriations bill included is designated as a separate division of the bill"), and concluded that CRS states the division formatting as an unqualified structural rule. The sentence actually begins on the previous page with "These minibus measures are usually formatted so that the text of the" -- "usually" is CRS's own word, not an added hedge. Verified by locating both halves in data/ref-text/record-crs-r47106-approps-overview.txt. The article keeps the qualifier because the source has it.

resolution: CONVERGED at pass 2. Two passes, each with an independent cross-model (Sonnet) hostile verifier run headless against the draft and the stored sources, plus an in-conversation hostile read by the drafting model.  PASS 1. Drafter self-audit found 18 items, all applied before any verifier reported: unsourced framing and metaphor stripped ("the divisions are sealed off from one another", "several statutes wearing one public law number", "the word regular is doing work there", "an omnibus is a vehicle for those regular acts, not a fifth type of them", "full-year CRs are uncommon", "which bills travel together is not settled until one of these laws is enacted", "the Senate has no equivalent lever" — the last replaced with the CRS sentence that actually states the Senate difference); source qualifiers restored where the draft had dropped them ("usually" on the division formatting); and the H.R. 8646 contrast rewritten from an absence-only claim into the positive structural fact (its text runs to Title I with no division heading, the structure a package carries one level down).  PASS 1 hostile source verifier (Sonnet): 0 BLOCKING, 6 non-blocking. Two were real ledger coverage gaps — the H.R. 5371 division-A and H.R. 7147 division-B titles were asserted in prose from bill texts that were not registered as ledger sources at all. Both bill texts are now registered and six rows added. One finding (the "usually" qualifier) was REJECTED with evidence and is recorded as such: the verifier read only the continuation of the R47106 sentence, which resumes on the next page, and missed that "usually" is CRS's own word. One framing sentence it flagged ("Each division also stands on its own terms") was cut.  PASS 1 editorial-compliance reviewer (Sonnet): 2 blocking, 5 non-blocking, all applied. The blocking pair were (a) the answer capsule's first sentence asserted that omnibus and minibus differ in size without saying which is which — the distinction only landed in sentence two, so an answer engine lifting the opening sentence got no answer; the capsule was rewritten to state the distinction first; and (b) the 1950 packaging experiment asserted Congress's motive ("intended to improve legislative efficiency") in the article's own voice while every other characterisation in the piece is attributed — now attributed to CRS.  PASS 2 hostile source verifier (Sonnet, fresh session, no prior-pass context): 0 FINDINGS, 0 blocking. It re-derived every vote tally, roll-call and record-vote number, public-law number, division letter, section number and date character-by-character against the stored records; cross-verified all twelve FY2026 act-to-law-and-division bindings two independent ways (each enacted bill's own table of contents, and H.R. 9770 section 101's list) and confirmed the four public laws sum to 3+3+5+1=12; confirmed each CRS claim traces to the correct one of the three distinct CRS products and each GAO claim to the correct one of the three glossary entries; confirmed the three non-law bills' claims resolve inside the engrossed files and not the introduced text that also exists under the same bill numbers; and independently confirmed the pass-1 "usually" REJECTION by reading both halves of the R47106 sentence across its page break.  PASS 2 editorial-compliance reviewer (Sonnet, fresh session): 2 blocking, 10 non-blocking. Nine non-blocking items were applied: the duplicated "amended separately in sequential order" clause was moved to the floor-vote section and cut from the minibus section; the recorded-votes bullet list was CUT entirely (it restated figures already given in place, and was the most tracker-like block in the article) with its two otherwise-unstated facts folded into the Senate paragraph; the committee-print sentence was split; H. Res. 977 is now glossed as the special rule for the bill, since H. Res. is a different designation from the H.R. used everywhere else; cloture, unanimous consent and the House Rules Committee now link to their own explainers; the minibus definition no longer says the same thing either side of a dash; "our own corpus" was replaced with plain "One example is"; and the closing section's throat-clearing transition was cut.  ONE PASS-2 COMPLIANCE FINDING IS RECORDED AND OVERRULED, NOT SILENTLY DROPPED — see notes. A second was overruled on the same basis (the reviewer applied ARTICLE-SPEC section 2.3's one-to-two-sentence nut-graf cap to what the commission specifies as a 120-160-word answer capsule; the capsule is a deliberate, documented departure and runs about 140 words). One further item was declined on the merits: the reviewer proposed renaming the heading "Where does a continuing resolution fit?" to "What is a continuing resolution?" for parallelism. Declined — the site already publishes continuing-resolution.html, and giving this article that heading would put the two pages in competition for the same query.
notes: SCOPE DECISION ON THE RECORD. The pass-2 editorial-compliance reviewer returned OVERALL: BLOCK on a single ground: ARTICLE_DRAFT_PROMPT RULE 2 says "Explainers make NO bill claims", and this explainer carries recorded votes, public-law numbers and division structures for eight bills in the corpus. The finding is recorded here in full because it is a legitimate reading of the rulebook and James or the QC pass may want to overrule the overrule.  It was NOT applied, for three reasons. First, the commission for this article (_personal/HANDOFF-OPUS-EXPLAINER-OMNIBUS-MINIBUS.md) directs the opposite in terms, and calls it the point of the piece: "The differentiator — use OUR audited corpus as the worked examples", naming these specific bills and requiring each to link to its /bill/<slug>/ page. It sets the guardrail in the same breath: "Bill FACTS are allowed only as receipt-bound examples." Second, that guardrail is met and machine-checked: every bill fact in the article is bound to a verbatim span in a stored source, and two independent hostile source audits found zero fabrications, zero contradictions and zero unsupported claims. Third, the reviewer was not shown the commission (a deliberate choice, so that it would judge the draft against the rulebook alone), so it applied RULE 2 without the instruction that overrides it here.  The reviewer's underlying risk argument was real and IS addressed. Bill facts go stale, which is why the tracker lane has a refresh loop and the explainer lane does not. Two mitigations: (1) the one bill still in play, H.R. 9770, now carries an explicit as-of-publication bound on its status rather than an open-ended present-tense claim, matching the phrasing already used for H.R. 7006; and (2) scripts/article-staleness.js extracts bill references from every articles/*.html by link and by bill code and flags any article whose referenced bill has a stageDate newer than the article date — so this page joins the staleness worklist automatically on publication, with no new machinery. The recorded-votes list was also cut, which removes the most tracker-like block and shrinks the bill-claim surface.  TWO PIPELINE DEFECTS WERE FOUND AND FIXED WHILE PRODUCING THIS ARTICLE, both unrelated to its prose. (1) scripts/verify-card-summaries.js hard-failed on any card whose article had not been published yet, which DEADLOCKED the entire first-publish path: publish-article.js requires the curated articles-index card BEFORE it will publish, and runs preflight (which runs this gate) BEFORE it moves the draft into articles/. Card-then-publish failed the gate; publish-then-card failed publish-article's own curated-entry check. It now resolves a card to drafts/ when articles/ has no such file, the same convention preflight.js isArticle() and article-ledger.js proseFile() already use. A card with neither a published article nor a draft still fails. The defect was latent because every publish since the gate shipped on 2026-08-27 has been a --refresh. (2) The article was initially drafted against superseded bill text: H.R. 7006, H.R. 8646 and H.R. 9770 all have Engrossed-in-House versions newer than what data/bill-text/ holds. Since the article asserts what PASSED THE HOUSE, all three now cite the engrossed text, fetched and stored as ledger sources. Every claim was re-verified and holds identically in the engrossed versions. data/bill-text/ was deliberately NOT overwritten — that is bill-lane data and re-fetching it changes analysis inputs.  BANKED FOR THE BILL LANE, NOT FIXED HERE: scripts/flag-version-drift.js only flags bills whose on-disk text is the INTRODUCED version (introducedOnDisk() matches Introduced/IH/IS only), so a bill sitting on REPORTED text with a known-different engrossed version is invisible to it. H.R. 8646 is a live instance — stage house, on-disk text Reported in House, versionChanges modified=6 added=2 — and npm run flag-drift reports 0 flagged. validate-batch's version-drift guard uses the same signal and has the same hole.
